title: LIVE GLOBAL OVATION AURORA FORECAST
freshness: LIVE / CURRENT FORECAST (OVATION Prime, hourly check)
noaa_source: NOAA/SWPC OVATION Prime aurora model (Aurora Viewline product family)
product_name: NOAA/SWPC OVATION Prime aurora model (Aurora Viewline product family)
variable: OVATION Prime auroral intensity, global 1-degree grid, both polar ovals
data_time_utc: obs 2026-10-11 03:54 AM EDT; forecast 2026-10-11 04:40 AM EDT
spatial_resolution_source: 1-degree global OVATION grid, bilinear to 0.1 deg canvas
spatial_resolution_rendered: 3600x1800 world canvas over lon [-180,180], lat [-90,90] (0.1 deg/px bilinear from the 1-degree source grid)
missing_data_treatment: intensity < 1.0 transparent; tropical model-background cells (|lat| < 40° and intensity < 5) masked as non-auroral noise — storm-level signal always paints, and the viewline is computed on unmasked source; full world equirectangular canvas lon -180..180 / lat -90..90 (3600x1800); missing source transparent, never zero-filled.
shoreline_mask: assets/great_lakes_watermask.png — shared NOAA medium-resolution shoreline water mask (nautical-chart compilation, mean-high-water datum; snapped + polygonized once, full vertex precision, antialiased). Overlay alpha is multiplied by this mask and edge RGB is bled into transparent pixels (anti-fringe for bilinear clients), so every product shares one shoreline.
attribution: Data: US NOAA. This project is not endorsed by NOAA. See DATA_SOURCES.md for exact products and endpoints.
legend_scale_html: Global OVATION auroral intensity, FIXED absolute scale 0–30+: LOWEST 0 (transparent) → 6 bright green (oval overhead) → 14 orange → 23 magenta (severe) → HIGHEST+ 30+ (violet extreme). Same intensity always shows the same color. White halo numbers are actual intensity at that spot. White viewline hugs the oval's farthest equatorward edge (dipping where coverage dips, like NOAA's own view line) (~56°N northern-oval farthest reach) — aurora may be visible low on the northern horizon from there under dark, clear skies. The line spans only longitudes where the oval actually reaches near it. Faint equatorial speckles are a known OVATION grid artifact, not aurora.
